source.title: Surgery: Mitigating Harmful Fine-Tuning for Large Language Models via Attention Sink
source.authors: Guo-Zhi Liu; Wei-Wei Lin; Tian-Sheng Huang; Ruichao Mo; Qi Mu; Xiu-Min Wang; Li Shen

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; some figure and equation formatting is garbled, but the relevant tables and prose are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests harmful fine-tuning with a different focus and reports harmful-output rates; it also probes attention-head contributions, but does not measure response-position KL or test opening-token bypasses.
record.gate_note: The paper tests fine-tuning with mixed harmful and benign data and reports harmful scores. Its head knockout results and head-count observations bear on safety mechanisms, but attention heads are not the weights or ranks named by V5, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. The paper's description of ConstrainedSFT and references to shallow alignment are background or baseline descriptions, not this study's tests of first-token KL, prefilling, suffixes, or decoding changes.
record.test_reason: A defense paper, but it reports vanilla-SFT harmful scores on Llama3-8B, Gemma2-9B and Qwen2.5-14B instruct models after fine-tuning on data with harmful fractions p=0.05–0.2 (50–250 harmful samples). These bear on V1. The measure is a BeaverTails moderation-classifier harmful score rather than Qi et al.'s HEx-PHI/GPT-4 judge, and there is no un-fine-tuned aligned baseline. The clean (p=0) SFT run is the only reference.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: they conclude that positive sink-divergence heads are associated with learning harmful patterns, and that the Surgery regularizer suppressing sink divergence lowers harmful score versus seven defenses while keeping comparable fine-tune accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Uses mixed benign and harmful fine-tuning datasets and reports harmful scores across ratios, sample counts, and instruction-tuned models; the paper does not establish an exact reproduction protocol for the original source.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper varies harmful-data ratio, training-set size, model, downstream task dataset, learning rate, and regularizer intensity; its reported defense outcomes vary across models and settings.

fits_no_version.finding: The count of heads with positive sink divergence rises with harmful ratio (553 to 580 for Lisa). Zeroing heads by sink-divergence sign changes harmful score, though the text is inconsistent on direction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attention-head groups defined by sink divergence are associated with learning harmful behavior during fine-tuning.

record.problems: The paper states that evaluation covers only open-source small-scale models and that early-layer suppression is relatively limited. The relevant harmful scores have no reported uncertainty estimates; some mechanism results are described from figures without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Results for the defense methods Surgery, Lisa, SafeGrad, ConstrainedSFT, AsFT, SPARD, and DSS were not cataloged individually where they only benchmark the proposed defense; the included SFT results and the explicit Lisa harmful-ratio examples cover the harmful-fine-tuning outcome relevant here. The paper's task-accuracy, system-overhead, regularizer-intensity, and learning-rate results do not measure a claim version.

untested.parts: Harmful-only fine-tuning; whether refusal is removed nearly entirely; comparison with the un-fine-tuned aligned model; few-shot (<50) harmful examples.
Entirely untested: clean SFT (HS 15.10) has no pre-fine-tuning reference.
Weight or rank localization not measured (only attention-head ablation).
ConstrainedSFT (token-wise constrained objective) is run only as a benchmarked baseline defense; not evaluated as a test of deepening.

missing.what: SFT harmful score by fine-tuning task at p=0.1: SST2 34.20, AGNEWS 31.00, GSM8K 27.60 (Llama3-8B)
SFT harmful score on other evaluation sets: HarmBench 28.75, SorryBench 30.91 (vs BeaverTails 27.60)
SFT harmful score by learning rate: 14.80 at 5e-7, 27.60 at 5e-6, 43.20 at 5e-5 (Llama3-8B)
SFT harmful-score curve up to p=0.5 (plotted only, no numbers in text)

record.verdict_notes: The V1 evidence is limited to the vanilla-SFT baseline of a defense paper. The harmful score is a moderation-classifier rate on BeaverTails, with no un-fine-tuned reference and no uncertainty reported. Duplicate rows: r3, r7 and r11 are the same run. The model name is inconsistent (Qwen2 vs Qwen2.5-14B).

versions.untested_parts: Uses mixed datasets with harmful fractions rather than harmful-only fine-tuning; does not establish that refusal is removed almost entirely.
The clean condition is reported, but no aligned, non-fine-tuned comparison establishes whether benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance.
Does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL across response positions.
Does not test compliant prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as bypasses.
Tests attention-head interventions, not localization in a small set of weights or ranks.
Does not test why safety would be shallow or whether data or objectives produce shallowness.
Does not train or evaluate safety distributed beyond the opening response tokens.

relationships.condition: Full-parameter SFT, lr 5e-6, 5 epochs, 50–250 harmful samples mixed into GSM8K; Llama3-8B, Gemma2-9B, Qwen2.5-14B instruct
relationships.reason: Harmful score rises from 15.10 (clean) to about 21–28%, far from near-total compliance. It plateaus with more harmful samples (24.1 at 250). Rows r2–r13; lr 5e-5 reaches 43.2 (text, Table 7).
relationships.display_finding: The harmful score rose from 15.10 with clean data to about 21–28% and plateaued with more harmful samples (24.1 at 250), while a higher learning rate of 5e-5 reached 43.2.

relation.reason: Tables 1–3 report harmful-response rates after harmful fine-tuning; Table 1 also provides a clean-SFT control.

tranche.reason: The vanilla-SFT controls test harmful fine-tuning's effect on safety using mixed downstream datasets and a moderation-classifier harmful score, rather than establishing an exact reproduction of the original protocol.

source_check.notes: r3, r7 and r11 repeat the default result. Clean-SFT controls are absent for Gemma2, Qwen and nondefault sample sizes; partial states there describe incomplete harmful compliance, not a measured increase against matched controls. The setup names Qwen2-14B, whereas Table 3 and its discussion name Qwen2.5-14B.
